title: Digital Creators Navigate Controversies, Legal Challenges, and Social Ethics Amidst Viral Incidents
summary: Recent weeks have seen a flurry of activity across the digital landscape, marked by influencer controversies, legal battles, and significant social discussions. A death hoax surrounding creator Krinjistan stirred social media, while Pranit More faced legal scrutiny for a controversial video, blaming his PR team. Pulkit Mani encountered threats and show cancellations following a political collaboration, leading to broader conversations about online harassment. These incidents, alongside public health concerns from major brands and a unique 'read-to-earn' initiative in Singapore, underscore the evolving complexities of the digital age and its impact on public discourse and individual lives.
article:
The digital world has been abuzz with a series of events ranging from influencer controversies and legal challenges to significant social and ethical debates. These incidents highlight the intricate dynamics of online presence, public perception, and accountability in the modern era.

A notable incident involved popular creator Krinjistan, who became the subject of a widespread death hoax. Rumors circulated online, citing a story by Instagram creator Parle 96, who posted "RIP People will always love you. Whenever pranksters will be discussed in India. Krinji's name will definitely be mentioned." However, these claims were swiftly countered by another friend, Trilochan, who asserted Krinjistan was alive. Further investigation by other digital personalities like Grox confirmed that no credible news or official reports substantiated the death claims. Given Krinjistan's reputation as a prankster, many social media users expressed skepticism, contributing to the rapid spread and subsequent debunking of the rumor.

In a high-profile legal development, influencer Pranit More appeared before the Supreme Court regarding the "370 Biryani" controversy. More placed the blame on his own PR team, asserting that the viral video was posted without his explicit approval. He informed the court that he became aware of the video's gravity only after an FIR was registered, prompting him to delete it immediately. More, who was traveling at the time of the posting, stated he had already issued a public apology to the NCW and intended to submit a written one. While expressing readiness to face trial, he requested the Supreme Court to consolidate the two FIRs filed against him in Maharashtra and Gurugram. The court is currently seeking responses from the Centre, Maharashtra, and Haryana regarding his plea.

Political collaborations also stirred significant reactions, as evidenced by comedian Pulkit Mani. Following an unexpected collaboration with Rahul Gandhi, which included mimicking Prime Minister Narendra Modi on stage, Mani reported receiving continuous threats. These threats led to the cancellation of his scheduled shows in Lucknow and Kanpur. Mani later used his Instagram platform to address and troll some of his detractors, highlighting the intense scrutiny and backlash public figures can face when engaging with political narratives. Separately, stand-up comedian Pulkit Pochar faced a case of mistaken identity, receiving a barrage of hateful messages intended for Pulkit Mani. Pochar humorously pointed out the error, suggesting that some news outlets might have confused their names without proper research.

Influencer Sourav Joshi weighed in on the issue of online negativity, addressing "unnecessary trolling." In his latest vlog, Joshi expressed his desire to undertake positive societal work but lamented the constant interference and judgment from online critics. He emphasized his resolve to live life on his own terms, asserting that he would not seek validation from anyone or society, trusting that "God is watching everything." His statement resonated with many who grapple with online harassment.

The broader issue of trolling also drew the attention of law enforcement. Following actor Salman Khan's strong stance against trolls during a Bigg Boss episode, the Delhi Police issued a public awareness notice. Their post cautioned against the lasting impact of online comments, stating, "A stray link is not just a comment. It can become a lasting impact. Think type respect." This initiative underscores the growing recognition of online trolling as a serious concern. In a related event, a Pakistani RJ publicly apologized to actress Katrina Kaif for body-shaming remarks made after her pregnancy. The RJ expressed deep remorse on Instagram, acknowledging the wrongness of his words and reflecting on the importance of respectful discourse.

Beyond the entertainment industry, the Asian Games brought attention to actor R Madhavan's son, an international swimmer. Despite setting the best Indian time by 0.5 seconds in a team event, he narrowly missed the finals by 0.2 seconds. However, he successfully qualified for the 50m backstroke final in an individual capacity. R Madhavan shared his appreciation for his son's efforts on Instagram, expressing pride through emojis.

In the tech sector, X (formerly Twitter) has initiated legal action against users for generating fake engagement. The company is suing two individuals from London, including Vivek Kumar Sen, alleging they earned $2.66 crores by running fake accounts, primarily crypto-related, to manipulate engagement. X is also demanding an additional $1000 from them to cover investigation and analysis fees, signaling a crackdown on deceptive practices on the platform.

Several incidents underscored societal challenges and public safety concerns. In Bihar, police took action following a widely publicized case that garnered significant internet outreach and celebrity condemnation. Three accused were arrested, and the main perpetrator was apprehended after an encounter where he sustained a leg injury. Amidst these developments, a Bihar minister faced criticism for a statement suggesting that "the entire world is not crime free" and that "isolated incidents keep happening," promising strict action.

A deeply insensitive incident occurred in Uttar Pradesh, where a man discovered people cooking chicken on his father's pyre after the funeral. The son reported the incident to the police, who apprehended one accused. The individual confessed to drinking alcohol at the site and deciding to cook chicken on the existing fire.

Public confrontations also played out in the digital sphere. A woman on Instagram shared a video from a train journey, where she confronted a man repeatedly flashing his phone number on his wallpaper towards her. The man appeared flustered, while an elderly woman beside the victim supported her. However, the woman later faced accusations on social media of seeking "likes and views." In response, she posted a follow-up video, deleting her original video, which had garnered 1.3 million views, to emphasize her sincerity in raising her voice against inappropriate behavior.

Consumer grievances highlighted issues with major brands. Viral videos circulated showing an insect in a Starbucks drink and a cockroach on a dinner table at JW Marriott. Customers in both instances demanded action from IAS Tukaram Munde, drawing attention to hygiene and quality control standards in prominent establishments.

In a unique legal challenge, a lawyer took PVR Inox to court after the multiplex refused to accept cash payment, insisting on UPI. The customer argued that cash is legal tender and cannot be refused. He demanded that if PVR Inox maintains a no-cash policy, it must be prominently displayed. He also sought copies of internal company policies regarding cash acceptance.

Finally, Singapore has launched an innovative "read-to-earn" initiative to combat "doom scrolling." A government website offers approximately 1000 coins, convertible to one Singaporean dollar, for daily reading. The Chief Executive of the National Library Board stated that the program aims to encourage reading, enhance attention span, critical thinking, empathy, and imagination, thereby reducing digital distractions.

These diverse events collectively paint a picture of a dynamic and often challenging digital and social landscape, where public figures, institutions, and individuals alike navigate evolving norms, legal frameworks, and ethical considerations.
tags: Influencer Controversy, Legal Disputes, Social Media Ethics, Digital Culture, Public Awareness
